diagnosis.narrative: The series carries a strong long-run trend. Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. A few outliers stand out (2 points, ~2% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.01), which favours a robust combination.

attempts.rationale: The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable model rankings (tau=0.01) and low predictability, suggesting a robust combination like the median over the full pool is a safe baseline to establish performance.

The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable model rankings (ranking tau=0.01), suggesting no single model dominates consistently. The median strategy performed well by being robust to this instability. To test if weighted averaging over the full pool can leverage individual model strengths despite the noise, I will evaluate a simple mean combination of all models.

The ranking stability is extremely low (tau=0.01) and error correlation is high, suggesting that robust aggregation like trimmed_mean or DBA may outperform simple mean/median by mitigating outlier models. Since median led slightly but the margin is statistically indistinguishable from mean, I will test a trimmed_mean to see if removing the worst-performing tails improves robustness against the unstable ranking.
Test if inverse error weighting on the full pool outperforms trimmed_mean by leveraging top models more heavily while maintaining diversity.
Testing DBA on full pool as a robust alternative to trimmed_mean/median given unstable rankings.
Testing softmax weighted combination on full pool to leverage all models with robust weighting against unstable rankings.

The current leader (a3) uses a trimmed mean on a small, carefully selected pool (pool4). The series has unstable rankings and strong seasonality, suggesting that robust aggregation over a diverse set of models is key. Since simple means and medians over the full pool performed worse than the trimmed mean on the subset, I will test a weighted combination using 'inverse_error' weights specifically on the same high-performing pool4 to see if adaptive weighting can outperform the static trimming on this specific group.

The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable rankings (ranking_tau=0.01), suggesting robust combinations are needed. The current leader uses inverse_error weighting on a small pool of top performers. I will test a mean combination on the full pool of diverse, low-correlation models to see if broad averaging outperforms the focused weighted approach given the high noise and instability.

The series has strong seasonality and a dominant trend, but unstable rankings (trend_strength=0.9982, ranking_tau=0.01) suggest robust combination is key. Leader a7 used inverse_error weighting on pool4. I have prepared handle w5 for top-k-per-horizon weighting on pool6 (the 5 best models by SMAPE). Testing this per-horizon adaptive strategy against the previous best to see if horizon-specific selection improves over static error-based weighting.

The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable model rankings (ranking tau ~0). Leader a7 uses inverse_error weighting on pool4, which worked well. I will test robust median combination on the same top-8 model pool (pool4) to see if it can match or beat the weighted approach given the instability.

The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable model rankings (ranking tau ~0), which favors robust combinations over weighted ones that might overfit to noise. The current leader uses a specific weighted pool, but the diagnostics suggest robustness is key. I will test `dba` (dynamic Bayesian averaging) on the top 8 models (pool4) as a robust alternative to mean/median that adapts to uncertainty, leveraging the stable correlation structure within that subset.

The series has strong seasonality and trend but unstable rankings (ranking_tau 0.01), suggesting robust combinations are needed. The current leader 'a7' uses a weighted combination on pool4. I will test a simpler, more robust approach: trimmed mean on the top-performing models from the error table to reduce variance from any single model's potential bias, specifically targeting the top 5-6 models that showed consistent low RMSE across windows.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9479. Series context: trend strength 0.9982 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.01); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.387.
